signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-30 reality-web pagination param validation gap)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/page.tsx:144 — `const currentPage = Number(searchParams.get('page') || 1);` does NOT validate the user-controlled `page` query param. `searchParams.get('page')` returns the raw string, so a non-numeric value like `?page=abc` is truthy, survives the `|| 1` guard (which only defaults null/empty), and `Number('abc')` yields `NaN`. Negative (`?page=-5`), zero (`?page=0`), and fractional (`?page=1.5`) values also pass through unclamped.

That `currentPage` flows straight into `useListings(filters, currentPage)` (page.tsx:145). frontend/packages/reality-api-client/src/listings/hooks.ts:22-25 buildQueryString then does `params.set('page', String(page))`, i.e. `page=NaN` (literal string 'NaN') is sent to reality-server's public listings endpoint. The React Query key `['listings', filters, NaN]` (hooks.ts:49) is also unstable/degenerate.

Impact: this is the PUBLIC, SEO-indexed search/results page (app/[locale]/listings). A trivially mistyped or crafted/bookmarked `?page=` value produces a broken request instead of gracefully defaulting to page 1 — either a forced full-page error state (the component destructures `isError` and renders the error branch) or, if the server leniently coerces, silently wrong paging. Either way an unvalidated user-facing input on a high-traffic public route yields degraded UX rather than a clamp-to-valid-page.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the Number()->NaN->String(NaN)='NaN'->API-param dataflow is confirmed by direct read; the one unconfirmed link is whether reality-server's page extractor rejects `page=NaN` with a 4xx (=> forced error state) or defaults it (=> silently-wrong-page) — both are user-facing defects, so the finding holds either way.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): clamp/validate the param, e.g. `const parsed = Number.parseInt(searchParams.get('page') ?? '', 10); const currentPage = Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed >= 1 ? parsed : 1;`. Single-file reality-web edit, verifies with pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck/test + biome; no backend coupling.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-30 reality-web API-body validation-boundary gap)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 — a shared-comparison URL (`?ids=...`) fans out to `await fetch(`${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}`)` per id and returns `response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` with NO runtime shape validation. The raw external API body is asserted to be a well-formed `ListingSummary` and then pushed into app state via `addToComparison(listing)` (L70).

This is the exact type-unsafe-cast-across-an-API-boundary pattern, and it is inconsistent with the app's own established convention: the sibling public detail page frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:79-92 documents that 'A 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body' and routes every listing body through `parseListingDetail(body)` to validate/coerce required nested fields (address.city, features, photos) before render, falling back to ListingNotFound on a bad body. The comparison ingestion path has no equivalent guard.

Why it is currently only LOW (defense-in-depth, not a live crash): ComparisonView.tsx happens to defensively guard its own field derefs (primaryPhoto ternary-guarded L276, address?.city optional-chained, area>0 before division). So a malformed body survives into state but does not crash today. The risk is regression-shaped: any future ComparisonView column that dereferences a required-but-actually-missing field (the currency path was already such a case, fixed 2026-09-21) crashes the comparison render, because the ingestion boundary provides no shape guarantee. Distinct from the 2026-09-19-2 comparison share-id ENCODING finding (that was about how ids are read from the URL; this is about validating the fetched listing BODY).
Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the unvalidated cast and the absence of any parse step are confirmed by direct read; classified LOW because current downstream consumers are defensive.

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): reuse/extract a ListingSummary normalizer (mirroring parseListingDetail) and validate each fetched body before `addToComparison`, dropping bad ones the same way the existing Promise.allSettled loop already drops failed fetches. Single-package reality-web edit, verifies with typecheck/test + biome.
